problems.title: Unrestricted six-dimensional corollary at residual one
problems.location: PDF/printed pp4-5, equation(1.8), Corollary1.6; proof p13
problems.source_claim: Every nonnegative u in the specified energy shell has distance at most C Gamma sqrt(|log Gamma|) in dimension6.
counterevidence: Local Theorem1.4 requires proximity and is not refuted by this example
Rate defined for all t>0 and corollary has no smallness condition
Inhomogeneous H-1 interpretation also admits counterexample by using B=||U²||H-1>5
problems.impact: False unrestricted dimension6 distance conclusion; n>=7 and small-residual logarithmic asymptotics not refuted.

correction.statement: Add Gamma<=epsilon<1 sufficiently small, or replace rate by Gamma sqrt(1+|log Gamma|).
correction.boundary: Conditional on a valid local theorem; independent proof defects remain.

problems.title: Raw inner products fail to define the asserted spectral projection
problems.location: PDF/printed p46 equations(6.4)-(6.6), p47 spectral gap; dependence pp49,13
problems.source_claim: beta_i=<rho1,Ui> and rho2=rho1-sum beta_i Ui imply rho2 orthogonal to Ui and Zi.
assumptions: Ui normalized as equation(1.3), not unit-norm vectors
arbitrarily small perturbation and weak interaction
problems.check: For Gram G, bubble moments of rho2 equal (I-G)b; tangent moments are -sum b_i<Ui,Zk>. In n6, rho1=tU gives rho2=t(1-A²)U and spectral quotient2>1.
problems.result: Invalid algebraic orthogonality and invalid invocation of strict spectral gap
counterevidence: A genuine joint projection can restore orthogonality but is not the printed formula
Single-bubble example is algebraic and does not require Q for empty pairs
For separated multiple bubbles G tends to A_n²I, so error persists
problems.impact: Lemma6.2 -> Lemma6.3 -> Proposition6.4 -> Lemma6.5/Lemma2.3 -> Theorem1.4. The theorem is not disproved.

correction.statement: Use tangent-orthogonal projected bubble directions or a joint Gram system, then rederive estimates.
correction.boundary: Gram inverse on bubble span alone does not enforce tangent orthogonality.

problems.title: Unweighted o(Q) inference fails for n>=12
problems.location: PDF/printed p50 final display of Lemma6.5; Proposition6.1 pp45-46; sharpness lower bound p52
problems.source_claim: ||grad rho0||^p+||grad rho1||^p is bounded by o(Q)+||f||^p using Propositions6.1/6.4.
problems.check: For n>=7 zeta_n(Q)^p=Q^(p²/2), and p²/2<1 for n>=12. At n12 exponent49/50. Section7 lower bound on projected correction and f=O(Q) rule out the asserted unweighted o(Q) conclusion for that sharp scale.
problems.result: Invalid dimensional inference in core proof; weighted conclusion not disproved
counterevidence: A weighted argument can restore required remainder
problems.impact: Lemma6.5 supplies oQ absorption in Lemma2.3 and Theorem1.4.

correction.statement: Integral |rho0|^p |Zk| <= C R^-4(p-1) integral VUk <= C R^-4(p-1)Q=oQ; rho1 <= C(Q^2p+||f||^p).
correction.boundary: Uses Proposition5.4, p45 weight bound, LemmaB.1 and Proposition6.4; does not repair P2 or certify entire theorem.

independent_acceptance.conclusion: All three Major findings are supported at their stated scope: an unrestricted six-dimensional corollary has an admissible exact counterexample, the printed decomposition lacks the orthogonality used by a core gap estimate, and the unweighted little-oh remainder fails from dimension twelve. Conditional local repairs are not presented as a completed proof of the main sharp stability theorem.

problem_checks.source: PDF pp4?5 equation1.8 and Corollary1.6; p13 closing proof
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: For n=6, nu=1, U=24/(1+|x|^2)^2 has A^2=||grad U||_2^2=1152*pi^3/5=S^6. Set c=(1+sqrt(1+4/A))/2 and u=cU. Then u>0, 1/2<c^2<36/25<3/2, so every energy-shell condition holds, while Gamma=Ac(c-1)=1. Every normalized bubble has norm A, giving exact distance (c-1)A=1/c>0 by reverse triangle inequality and equality at U. Yet zeta6(1)=0. The displayed corollary does not impose small residual or exclude nu=1.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: This does not refute the sufficiently small-residual local theorem. If H^-1 is inhomogeneous, B=||U^2||_H^-1 >= A sqrt(12/17)>5 and choosing c with Bc(c-1)=1 gives the same counterexample. Requiring Gamma<=epsilon<1, or using t sqrt(1+|log t|), supports a globalization only conditional on the local theorem; that conditional status is retained.

problem_checks.source: PDF p46 equations6.4?6.6; p47 spectral-gap use; p49 Proposition6.4 and p13 theorem closing
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: With b_k=<rho1,U_k> and G_ki=<U_i,U_k>, the printed beta_i=b_i leaves bubble moments (I-G)b. G has diagonal A_n^2, not one, and positive off-diagonal interactions. Subtracting these bubble directions also generally destroys tangent orthogonality. In the exact one-bubble test u=(1+t)U, rho0=0, rho1=tU and <U,Z>=0, so rho2=t(1-A^2)U. Its spectral quotient is p=2, contradicting the invoked gap coefficient <1. Projecting a bubble direction into the tangent-orthogonal complement gives the same obstruction in sufficiently separated multi-bubble configurations.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: This disproves the displayed decomposition properties and their use, not the conclusion of Lemma6.2 or the main theorem. A diagonal normalization alone is insufficient; G^-1 fixes only bubble moments. A joint bubble-and-tangent projection and new multiplier/coefficient estimates are required. The full repair is not verified.

problem_checks.source: PDF p50 last line of Lemma6.5 proof; pp45?46 Proposition6.1; pp50?52 sharpness; pp43?45 weighted inputs
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: For n>=7, the cited energy bound gives ||grad rho0||^p <= C Q^(p^2/2). At n=12, p=7/5 and p^2/2=49/50<1, so Q^(49/50)/Q diverges. The exponent decreases for larger n. The two-bubble sharpness construction has residual O(Q) and, after fixing L and taking R large, ||grad rho0|| bounded below by a constant times zeta_n(Q), ruling out the claimed global unweighted o(Q)+O(||f||^p) bound in this range.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: The weighted integral may still be small. Using |rho0|<=CW, W^p<=C R^(-4(p-1))V, int VU_k<=CQ and |Z_k|<=CU_k gives the needed integral O(R^(-4(p-1))Q)=o(Q). The rho1 term follows from Proposition6.4 as O(Q^(2p)+||f||^p), conditional on repairing P2. The repair restores this weighted step, not every upstream bubble-tree estimate.
